## Clean Windows app: new setup in Rust, no more sandbox alarms
A sandbox analysis (Hatching Triage, score 7/10) showed behaviour that looks like malware. Every point was traced to its cause and fixed at the cause, nothing is hidden or packed away.

- **New Windows setup, written in Rust:** `Streyn.exe` is now a small Rust program instead of an NSIS installer. It no longer unpacks plug-in DLLs into `%TEMP%`, no longer scans running processes, no longer borrows the Explorer's rights to start the app and never asks for admin rights. It installs for your user only into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Streyn` (like Spotify), checks both program files against a checksum before writing anything and starts Streyn
- **Updates without closing other programs:** a running Streyn is not touched; its file is renamed and the new version is used on the next start
- **Uninstall like Spotify:** Settings → Apps → Installed apps → Streyn runs `Streyn.exe --uninstall`. It removes the program files, shortcuts and its own entry, your settings and offline downloads stay
- **Offline server only when needed:** the desktop app no longer starts `streyn-server.exe` just to ask whether something was downloaded. It only starts once you download a playlist, and it now always ends together with the app, also after a crash
- **No network lookups in offline mode:** the offline server listens on 127.0.0.1 only and no longer reads the computer's network setup
- **yt-dlp on Windows without temporary DLLs:** a Windows server now uses yt-dlp's folder build, installed once in its data folder, instead of the single-file build that unpacked a Python runtime into `%TEMP%` on every song

## Install
- **Windows:** download `Streyn.exe` once and run it (or use Update in the app). It replaces the old installation in the same folder
- **Server:** Settings → Updates → Update now (or run the Proxmox script)
- **Android / Linux:** nothing to install, the apps pick it up from the server
